content.content:
360	**Level 1: image search (DEVDESK-299, IS-01; Open Tags DEVDESK-300, IS-11).**
361	The browser has three states: `browserStateInput` (form), `browserStateImages`
362	(level 1, appended last in the `iota` list) and `browserStateTags` (level 2).
363	
364	*The form's buttons.* `formButtons()` (`browser_form.go`) is the single source
365	of the buttons: the keyboard, the rendering (`renderFormButtons`, one line) and
366	the header (`FormEnter`) all read it. Without a `Searcher` there is one button,
367	`Browse Tags` (action `actionSearch`). With one there are two, `Search`
368	(`actionSearch`) then `Open Tags` (`actionOpenTags`).
369	
370	*Field indices.* Repository is `brFieldRepo` (0); the picker checkboxes are
371	1..n (n = `len(b.rows)`); the buttons follow: `brFieldButton(i)` = `1 + n + i`,
372	and `brFieldLast()` is the last button. `focusedButton()` maps the focus back to
373	a button (false on Repository or a checkbox). `down` stops at `brFieldLast()`.
374	
375	*Validation.* `submit(action)` is common to both actions: an empty name starts
376	nothing; no registry checked sends `RegistryBrowserWarnMsg{"No registry
377	selected"}`, which the `Model` shows as a footer warning (the browser has no
378	footer; this also applies to a name that contains `/`, where the tag flow used
379	to refuse silently). Then `actionOpenTags` always goes to `startTagLookup`
380	(the former code extracted as is, name as typed). `actionSearch` follows the
381	IS-01 rule: a name with no `/` goes to `startImageSearch` when `b.searcher !=
382	nil`, anything else to `startTagLookup`. `enter` on Repository runs
383	`actionSearch`; `enter` on a button runs that button's action; `enter` on a
384	checkbox only advances the focus. The selection applies to both actions.
385	
386	*Header.* `FormEnter()` returns the label and the lit state of the header's
387	single `enter` entry. The label follows the focus: `Search` on Repository and
388	on the Search button (`Browse tags` without a `Searcher`), `Open tags` on the
389	Open Tags button. `enter` is lit on Repository (Rule 130: it submits there) and
390	on a button, and greyed on a checkbox.
391	
392	*Help.* `registryBrowserHelpBody(searchEnabled)` (`view.go`) depends on the
393	mode (Rule 114): without a `Searcher` it names Browse Tags only; with one it
394	describes Search, Open Tags and the shared selection, and the level 1 sentence.
395	
396	**`defaultImageSearcher` is `ByRegistry(HubSearcher{}, CatalogSearcher{})` in
397	production (DEVDESK-301, IS-02; catalog since DEVDESK-306, IS-03), so level 1
398	and Open Tags are active.** `newRegistryBrowser`
399	copies it into `b.searcher`. Tests do not use it: `TestMain`
400	(`ociresources_test.go`) saves it in `productionImageSearcher` and sets
401	`defaultImageSearcher` to `nil` for the whole suite (no test may reach the real
402	Hub), and tests inject a fake with `withImageSearcher`.
403	`TestProductionWiresTheHubSearcher` reads the saved value. `internal/app`
404	injects nothing: its tests avoid level 1 by typing a name with a `/`.
405	
406	`startImageSearch` runs one `searchImagesCmd` per checked registry, with
407	`targetFor(entry)` (same credentials as the tag flow, `credsFor`). Each command
408	wraps the lot's context in `context.WithTimeout(ctx, imageSearchDeadline)`:
409	`imageSearchDeadline` is 15 s **per registry**, the whole walk included, on top
410	of the 15 s client timeout per request (see the limit above). A registry's
411	answer arrives as `ImageSearchResultMsg{Gen, EntryKey, Images, Partial, Err}`
412	and `AddImageResults` takes it (false when stale; `pendingSearches` never goes
413	under 0).
414	
415	**Verdicts per registry (DEVDESK-303, IS-12).** `AddImageResults` calls
416	`imagesearch.Classify` in `Update`, never in the `Cmd` (Rule 110), and stores the
417	result in `RegistryBrowser.outcomes`, keyed by `EntryKey`. The map is reset by
418	`startImageSearch`, so it holds one lot only; a registry with no entry is still
419	pending. Only an `ok` verdict appends rows. `Outcome(entryKey)` reads one
420	verdict (false while pending). `Model.RegistryBrowserOutcomes()` returns a copy
421	of the map, or nil when the browser is closed; it is for the tests and for IS-13.
422	
423	**Level 1 header summary (DEVDESK-305, IS-13).** `searchHeaderInfo`
424	(`browser_summary.go`, called from `GetHeaderInfo`) says what the lot did, one
425	header line per class, in this order: `Images` (the row count, always), then
426	`Pending` (a count, live lot) or `Interrupted` (names, the lot was abandoned
427	with the left arrow before they answered), `Failed` (red), `Refused`, `Partial`
428	(orange), `Cached only` (orange, DEVDESK-308, IS-14), `No result` (dim) and `Skipped` (dim, catalog not walked because the
429	query is shorter than `imagesearch.CatalogMinQueryRunes`). A class with nothing
430	to say has no line, so a lot where every registry answered shows only `Images`.
431	`summarizeSearch` (pure) sorts the lot's keys into the classes. A name is the
432	Registry column's label (`entryLabel`: alias, else URL, else key), in form order.
433	`Partial` lists registries cut at a cap, `No result` those that answered with
434	nothing (Skipped excluded). A registry that is both partial and empty appears
435	on both lines, on purpose.
436	
437	`Cached only` lists the registries whose list is limited to cached content: a
438	`provider: nexus` + `kind: group` entry, or a member of such a group (a
439	discovered member, or a declared entry whose `parent` is the slug of one).
440	`config.IsNexusGroup` and `listsCacheOnly` decide, once, into
441	`browserRegistryEntry.cachedOnly`; `summarizeSearch` reads it by entry key
442	(`entryCachedOnly`, not by slug: members share their group's slug). A concerned
443	registry that answered with no result is marked ` (no result)` on that line and
444	is not on `No result`, so `No result: quay` means absent from the registry and
445	`Cached only: nexus (no result)` means absent from the cache. A concerned
446	partial registry appears on `Partial` and on `Cached only`. Failed, Refused and
447	Skipped win: no mention. Docker Hub, generic registries and a Nexus outside a
448	group never get the line. `Cached only` and `Skipped` exclude each other, which
449	keeps the budget below. Nexus's cache-only behavior comes from secondary
450	sources and is not verified on a real Nexus (to confirm in IS-16).
451	
452	Each name list is fitted by `fitNames` to the room a value has
453	(`shortcut.HeaderValueWidth`), so the `+N` is never lost: all the names, else
454	the first k names then `+N`, else `+N` alone. `Skipped` carries the hint
455	` (type N+ characters)`, which is the first thing dropped when the header is
456	narrow. The summary has a budget of `shortcut.HeaderRows` (7) lines, `Images`
457	included; classes after the sixth are left out (with `Cached only` the seven
458	classes fit only because `Pending`/`Interrupted` and `Skipped`/`Cached only`
459	exclude each other). Before the first
460	`WindowSizeMsg` nothing is abbreviated. At level 2 (tags) the header is the
461	usual tag count.
462	
463	Limit, accepted (R2): below about 50 columns `HeaderValueWidth` is 0 or 1,
464	nothing fits, `fitNames` returns `+N` anyway and the router clips it.
465	
466	Logging, by verdict, through `logSearchOutcome` (the alias falls back to the
467	entry key):
468	- `failed`: `ERROR [oci_resources] image search on <alias>: <cause>`;
469	- `refused`: `INFO [oci_resources] image search on <alias>: unsupported or
470	  refused: <cause>` (a refusal is expected for dhi.io and for a registry whose catalog
471	  is disabled, forbidden or not under the entry's prefix, so it does not fill
472	  the error log);
473	- `ok` and `no result`: nothing.
474	
475	The cause is `searchErrorCause(err)`: a `*url.Error` keeps only its Op and Err
476	(the URL carries the typed text and can carry credentials), then
477	`jobs.SafeCause`. Nothing else reaches the log. Nothing reaches the screen
478	either, and no error text reaches `:jobs` (Rule 128).
479	
480	Level 1 shows `searchTable` (`datatable.Model[searchRow]`, built by
481	`newSearchTable`, also used by `ActivityTables` as `oci/registry-search`).
482	Columns: the activity column (`IndicatorColumn`, always `Idle`, `IconDocker` in
483	the `IconRoleImage` role), Name (flex, searchable), Registry, Stars (empty when
484	`HasStars` is false), Official (`official` or empty) and Description
485	(searchable). All cells are plain text (Rule 122). When the terminal narrows,
486	Description, then Stars, then Official leave whole (`Optional`, with
487	`DropFirst` on Description and Stars); at 60 columns only the activity column,
488	Name and Registry remain, and the line spans width-2 at every width (Rule 116). Results are
489	ordered by `sortSearchRows` (`browser_images_order.go`), a pure function of the
490	rows and the typed name (`RegistryBrowser.searchQuery`, set by
491	`startImageSearch`), so the order never depends on which registry answered
492	first. Ranks (`imagesearch.MatchTier`, case-insensitive): 0 name equals the query, 1 last
493	path segment equals it, 2 last segment starts with it, 3 name contains it, 4 no
494	match; then name, registry alias, `EntryKey` and `Repo`. Stars play no part. The
495	cursor follows the selected row by `EntryKey` + `Repo`, never by index:
496	`rebuildSearchTable` remembers the selection before `SetItems` and puts the
497	cursor back with `SetCursor` (all in `Update()`, `datatable` untouched). With
498	nothing selected (empty table, so also a new search, which starts from
499	`SetItems(nil)`) the cursor goes to the first row received; a row that
500	disappears leaves the cursor where it is. Rule 139: an empty table keeps its
501	header. The header reads `Images: <visible rows>`, the title carries the typed
502	name (`... > Registry Browser > <name>`) at level 1 (once `→` opens a row, the
503	title carries that row's name, see below), and the footer shows the shared
504	activity dot with `Searching registries...` while `pendingSearches > 0`. Once
505	the search is done, the footer describes the selected row (`Status.Detail`): its
506	full reference (`searchRow.ref`, built by `searchRowReference`: host, then
507	`Repo`; Docker Hub always `docker.io`) and the registry label (`Image <ref> on
508	<label>`, no ` on` when the label is empty); `Searching registries...` keeps
509	priority. The keys are in
510	`ui-components.md`.
511	
512	**`→` at level 1: open the tags of a row (DEVDESK-304).** `→` opens the usual
513	tag table for the row under the cursor (`openSelectedImageTags`). It sends one
514	request, to the row's own registry (`selectedImage` finds the entry by
515	`EntryKey`), for the row's final repository: `searchRow.img.Repo` is passed as
516	is, with no prefix and no `library/` added again (`normalizeRepoForRegistry` and
517	`joinRepoPrefix` run only in `startTagLookup`, the typed-name flow). Both flows
518	build the request through `newTagRequest` (alias, API address, `credsFor`) and
519	open the lot through `startTagRequests`, so the tag table, the pull and the scan
520	references are the same as in the full-name flow. `startTagRequests` also
521	records where the table came from: `tagsFromSearch` (true for `→`) and
522	`tagsImage` (the row's `Name`, empty for the full-name flow). `GetTitle` shows
523	`tagsImage` in the tags state instead of the typed name.
524	
525	- **No row.** `imageDrillIn` (one computation for the header and the handler,
526	  Rule 130) reports `reasonNoImage`. `→` changes nothing and warns through
527	  `RegistryBrowserWarnMsg`: footer Warn `No image selected`. The `→ Open tags`
528	  shortcut is greyed.
529	- **Failed listing.** `handleMultiRegistryTagsLoaded`, when `tagsFromSearch` is
530	  set, leaves the table with its header only (Rule 139), shows `tagsLoadFailedText`
531	  (`Could not load tags`) as a 3 s footer Error, and logs
532	  `ERROR [oci_resources] registry tags on <alias>: <cause>` where the cause comes
533	  from `searchErrorCause`: no credentials, no URL. The full-name flow is
534	  unchanged and silent on screen (it logs `registry tags <repo> from <url>`).
535	- **Search in flight.** `→` while the level 1 search still runs cancels it
536	  (the browser has one lot at a time, `beginRequests`): the rows already shown
537	  stay, the late ones are dropped. Unchanged by IS-03, although catalog walks
538	  make searches slower and `→` will cut them more often: the user reopens the
539	  search. Keeping the lot alive behind the tags would be a separate story.
540	
541	**Back to level 1 (DEVDESK-307).** `←` and `esc` on the tag table call
542	`leaveTags`, which returns no Cmd (so no new request). Typing in the tag filter
543	comes first: `esc` closes the bar and `←` stays in the text field. `leaveTags`
544	reads the origin from `tagsFromSearch`:
545	
546	- **Opened with `→`:** back to level 1 (`browserStateImages`), untouched. The
547	  rows, the sort order, the cursor and the filter are the ones the user left;
548	  `searchTable` is neither emptied nor rebuilt (`rebuildSearchTable` would move
549	  the cursor).
550	- **Opened by full name:** back to the form (`browserStateInput`), focus on the
551	  Open Tags button as before.
552	
553	On both origins `leaveTags` calls `abandonLot`: it cancels the tag lot, takes a
554	new generation and zeroes `pendingSearches`, so a late tag answer or failure is
555	dropped by the generation test and cannot show `Could not load tags` over the
556	form or level 1 (this closes open point 5 of D132). It also resets the tag
557	filters (`registryFilter`, `filterInput`, `filterActive`) and `tagsImage`, so
558	the title does not keep a stale `[alias]` or image name. Level 1 itself:
559	`←` goes back to the form (`backToForm`, which also calls `abandonLot`) and
560	keeps the typed name and the selected registries, even with a confirmed filter
561	query. `esc` still clears a confirmed query first. While the filter bar is being
562	typed in, `esc` closes the bar and `←` stays in the text field. There is no `←`
563	entry in the shortcuts header: `esc Go back` already shows in both states
564	(Rule 130, D133).
565	
566	**Networks, Volumes and Registries (DEVDESK-153, A-09b).** Each takes
567	`datatable.IndicatorColumn` as column 0. Rows carry no `components.RowActivity`:
568	the datatable reads its own busy marker (`MarkBusy`), and the column's
569	`Indicator` function returns `Idle` (or `Running` when `registryRow.refreshing`
570	is set). A remove, login or logout in flight is that marker, reported as
571	`Running` with its label (`BusyLabel`). On these three tables a failure never

on a button, and greyed on a checkbox.

*Help.* `registryBrowserHelpBody(searchEnabled)` (`view.go`) depends on the
mode (Rule 114): without a `Searcher` it names Browse Tags only; with one it
describes Search, Open Tags and the shared selection, and the level 1 sentence.

**`defaultImageSearcher` is `ByRegistry(HubSearcher{}, CatalogSearcher{})` in
production (DEVDESK-301, IS-02; catalog since DEVDESK-306, IS-03), so level 1
and Open Tags are active.** `newRegistryBrowser`
copies it into `b.searcher`. Tests do not use it: `TestMain`
(`ociresources_test.go`) saves it in `productionImageSearcher` and sets
`defaultImageSearcher` to `nil` for the whole suite (no test may reach the real
Hub), and tests inject a fake with `withImageSearcher`.
`TestProductionWiresTheHubSearcher` reads the saved value. `internal/app`
injects nothing: its tests avoid level 1 by typing a name with a `/`.

`startImageSearch` runs one `searchImagesCmd` per checked registry, with
`targetFor(entry)` (same credentials as the tag flow, `credsFor`). Each command
wraps the lot's context in `context.WithTimeout(ctx, imageSearchDeadline)`:
`imageSearchDeadline` is 15 s **per registry**, the whole walk included, on top
of the 15 s client timeout per request (see the limit above). A registry's
answer arrives as `ImageSearchResultMsg{Gen, EntryKey, Images, Partial, Err}`
and `AddImageResults` takes it (false when stale; `pendingSearches` never goes
under 0).

**Verdicts per registry (DEVDESK-303, IS-12).** `AddImageResults` calls
`imagesearch.Classify` in `Update`, never in the `Cmd` (Rule 110), and stores the
result in `RegistryBrowser.outcomes`, keyed by `EntryKey`. The map is reset by
`startImageSearch`, so it holds one lot only; a registry with no entry is still
pending. Only an `ok` verdict appends rows. `Outcome(entryKey)` reads one
verdict (false while pending). `Model.RegistryBrowserOutcomes()` returns a copy
of the map, or nil when the browser is closed; it is for the tests and for IS-13.

**Level 1 header summary (DEVDESK-305, IS-13).** `searchHeaderInfo`
(`browser_summary.go`, called from `GetHeaderInfo`) says what the lot did, one
header line per class, in this order: `Images` (the row count, always), then
`Pending` (a count, live lot) or `Interrupted` (names, the lot was abandoned
with the left arrow before they answered), `Failed` (red), `Refused`, `Partial`
(orange), `Cached only` (orange, DEVDESK-308, IS-14), `No result` (dim) and `Skipped` (dim, catalog not walked because the
query is shorter than `imagesearch.CatalogMinQueryRunes`). A class with nothing
to say has no line, so a lot where every registry answered shows only `Images`.
`summarizeSearch` (pure) sorts the lot's keys into the classes. A name is the
Registry column's label (`entryLabel`: alias, else URL, else key), in form order.
`Partial` lists registries cut at a cap, `No result` those that answered with
nothing (Skipped excluded). A registry that is both partial and empty appears
on both lines, on purpose.

`Cached only` lists the registries whose list is limited to cached content: a
`provider: nexus` + `kind: group` entry, or a member of such a group (a
discovered member, or a declared entry whose `parent` is the slug of one).
`config.IsNexusGroup` and `listsCacheOnly` decide, once, into
`browserRegistryEntry.cachedOnly`; `summarizeSearch` reads it by entry key
(`entryCachedOnly`, not by slug: members share their group's slug). A concerned
registry that answered with no result is marked ` (no result)` on that line and
is not on `No result`, so `No result: quay` means absent from the registry and
`Cached only: nexus (no result)` means absent from the cache. A concerned
partial registry appears on `Partial` and on `Cached only`. Failed, Refused and
Skipped win: no mention. Docker Hub, generic registries and a Nexus outside a
group never get the line. `Cached only` and `Skipped` exclude each other, which
keeps the budget below. Nexus's cache-only behavior comes from secondary
sources and is not verified on a real Nexus (to confirm in IS-16).

Each name list is fitted by `fitNames` to the room a value has
(`shortcut.HeaderValueWidth`), so the `+N` is never lost: all the names, else
the first k names then `+N`, else `+N` alone. `Skipped` carries the hint
` (type N+ characters)`, which is the first thing dropped when the header is
narrow. The summary has a budget of `shortcut.HeaderRows` (7) lines, `Images`
included; classes after the sixth are left out (with `Cached only` the seven
classes fit only because `Pending`/`Interrupted` and `Skipped`/`Cached only`
exclude each other). Before the first
`WindowSizeMsg` nothing is abbreviated. At level 2 (tags) the header is the
usual tag count.

Limit, accepted (R2): below about 50 columns `HeaderValueWidth` is 0 or 1,
nothing fits, `fitNames` returns `+N` anyway and the router clips it.

Logging, by verdict, through `logSearchOutcome` (the alias falls back to the
entry key):
- `failed`: `ERROR [oci_resources] image search on <alias>: <cause>`;
- `refused`: `INFO [oci_resources] image search on <alias>: unsupported or
  refused: <cause>` (a refusal is expected for dhi.io and for a registry whose catalog
  is disabled, forbidden or not under the entry's prefix, so it does not fill
  the error log);
- `ok` and `no result`: nothing.

The cause is `searchErrorCause(err)`: a `*url.Error` keeps only its Op and Err
(the URL carries the typed text and can carry credentials), then
`jobs.SafeCause`. Nothing else reaches the log. Nothing reaches the screen
either, and no error text reaches `:jobs` (Rule 128).

Level 1 shows `searchTable` (`datatable.Model[searchRow]`, built by
`newSearchTable`, also used by `ActivityTables` as `oci/registry-search`).
Columns: the activity column (`IndicatorColumn`, always `Idle`, `IconDocker` in
the `IconRoleImage` role), Name (flex, searchable), Registry, Stars (empty when
`HasStars` is false), Official (`official` or empty) and Description
(searchable). All cells are plain text (Rule 122). When the terminal narrows,
Description, then Stars, then Official leave whole (`Optional`, with
`DropFirst` on Description and Stars); at 60 columns only the activity column,
Name and Registry remain, and the line spans width-2 at every width (Rule 116). Results are
ordered by `sortSearchRows` (`browser_images_order.go`), a pure function of the
rows and the typed name (`RegistryBrowser.searchQuery`, set by
`startImageSearch`), so the order never depends on which registry answered
first. Ranks (`imagesearch.MatchTier`, case-insensitive): 0 name equals the query, 1 last
path segment equals it, 2 last segment starts with it, 3 name contains it, 4 no
match; then name, registry alias, `EntryKey` and `Repo`. Stars play no part. The
cursor follows the selected row by `EntryKey` + `Repo`, never by index:
`rebuildSearchTable` remembers the selection before `SetItems` and puts the
cursor back with `SetCursor` (all in `Update()`, `datatable` untouched). With
nothing selected (empty table, so also a new search, which starts from
`SetItems(nil)`) the cursor goes to the first row received; a row that
disappears leaves the cursor where it is. Rule 139: an empty table keeps its
header. The header reads `Images: <visible rows>`, the title carries the typed
name (`... > Registry Browser > <name>`) at level 1 (once `→` opens a row, the
title carries that row's name, see below), and the footer shows the shared
activity dot with `Searching registries...` while `pendingSearches > 0`. Once
the search is done, the footer describes the selected row (`Status.Detail`): its
full reference (`searchRow.ref`, built by `searchRowReference`: host, then
`Repo`; Docker Hub always `docker.io`) and the registry label (`Image <ref> on
<label>`, no ` on` when the label is empty); `Searching registries...` keeps
priority. The keys are in
`ui-components.md`.

**`→` at level 1: open the tags of a row (DEVDESK-304).** `→` opens the usual
tag table for the row under the cursor (`openSelectedImageTags`). It sends one
request, to the row's own registry (`selectedImage` finds the entry by
`EntryKey`), for the row's final repository: `searchRow.img.Repo` is passed as
is, with no prefix and no `library/` added again (`normalizeRepoForRegistry` and
`joinRepoPrefix` run only in `startTagLookup`, the typed-name flow). Both flows
build the request through `newTagRequest` (alias, API address, `credsFor`) and
open the lot through `startTagRequests`, so the tag table, the pull and the scan
references are the same as in the full-name flow. `startTagRequests` also
records where the table came from: `tagsFromSearch` (true for `→`) and
`tagsImage` (the row's `Name`, empty for the full-name flow). `GetTitle` shows
`tagsImage` in the tags state instead of the typed name.

- **No row.** `imageDrillIn` (one computation for the header and the handler,
  Rule 130) reports `reasonNoImage`. `→` changes nothing and warns through
  `RegistryBrowserWarnMsg`: footer Warn `No image selected`. The `→ Open tags`
  shortcut is greyed.
- **Failed listing.** `handleMultiRegistryTagsLoaded`, when `tagsFromSearch` is
  set, leaves the table with its header only (Rule 139), shows `tagsLoadFailedText`
  (`Could not load tags`) as a 3 s footer Error, and logs
  `ERROR [oci_resources] registry tags on <alias>: <cause>` where the cause comes
  from `searchErrorCause`: no credentials, no URL. The full-name flow is
  unchanged and silent on screen (it logs `registry tags <repo> from <url>`).
- **Search in flight.** `→` while the level 1 search still runs cancels it
  (the browser has one lot at a time, `beginRequests`): the rows already shown
  stay, the late ones are dropped. Unchanged by IS-03, although catalog walks
  make searches slower and `→` will cut them more often: the user reopens the
  search. Keeping the lot alive behind the tags would be a separate story.

**Back to level 1 (DEVDESK-307).** `←` and `esc` on the tag table call
`leaveTags`, which returns no Cmd (so no new request). Typing in the tag filter
comes first: `esc` closes the bar and `←` stays in the text field. `leaveTags`
reads the origin from `tagsFromSearch`:

- **Opened with `→`:** back to level 1 (`browserStateImages`), untouched. The
  rows, the sort order, the cursor and the filter are the ones the user left;
  `searchTable` is neither emptied nor rebuilt (`rebuildSearchTable` would move
  the cursor).
- **Opened by full name:** back to the form (`browserStateInput`), focus on the
  Open Tags button as before.

On both origins `leaveTags` calls `abandonLot`: it cancels the tag lot, takes a
new generation and zeroes `pendingSearches`, so a late tag answer or failure is
dropped by the generation test and cannot show `Could not load tags` over the
form or level 1 (this closes open point 5 of D132). It also resets the tag
filters (`registryFilter`, `filterInput`, `filterActive`) and `tagsImage`, so
the title does not keep a stale `[alias]` or image name. Level 1 itself:
`←` goes back to the form (`backToForm`, which also calls `abandonLot`) and
keeps the typed name and the selected registries, even with a confirmed filter
query. `esc` still clears a confirmed query first. While the filter bar is being
typed in, `esc` closes the bar and `←` stays in the text field. There is no `←`
entry in the shortcuts header: `esc Go back` already shows in both states
(Rule 130, D133).

**Networks, Volumes and Registries (DEVDESK-153, A-09b).** Each takes
`datatable.IndicatorColumn` as column 0. Rows carry no `components.RowActivity`:
the datatable reads its own busy marker (`MarkBusy`), and the column's
`Indicator` function returns `Idle` (or `Running` when `registryRow.refreshing`
is set). A remove, login or logout in flight is that marker, reported as
`Running` with its label (`BusyLabel`). On these three tables a failure never
leaves a `⊗` dot, only a footer message. On Registries, a group whose members are being discovered
(`refreshingGroups`) is `Running` too, and the Members cell is static dim text:

## DEVDESK-309 (IS-05) et DEVDESK-310 (IS-06) : plan d'implémentation

Je n'ai rien modifié. Ce plan s'appuie sur le code de `main` (f74f306d).

### Questions bloquantes

**Q1. Comment lire « un second tour sur une colonne inverse l'ordre » (IS-05 c.1) ?**
- (a) Le cycle de `datatable.CycleSort`, déjà utilisé par la table des tags et partout ailleurs (Rule 111) : Name ▲, Name ▼, Registry ▲, Registry ▼, Stars ▼, Stars ▲, puis l'ordre par défaut. On ne touche pas à `datatable`.
- (b) La lecture littérale : un premier tour sur les trois colonnes dans un sens, puis l'ordre par défaut, puis un second tour dans l'autre sens. Il faut alors étendre `datatable`, qui est un composant partagé, et le comportement diffère de toutes les autres tables (Rule 101).
- **Je recommande (a)** ; le plan ci-dessous la suppose.

**Q2. Une nouvelle recherche doit-elle aussi effacer le filtre `/` confirmé et le filtre `r` ?**
- Aujourd'hui, une requête `/` confirmée reste active d'une recherche à l'autre (`startImageSearch` ne touche pas la barre), et elle peut masquer les nouveaux résultats.
- Le niveau 2, lui, remet tout à zéro (`startTagRequests`).
- **Je recommande oui** : effacer requête, filtre de registre et jeton, comme l'ordre de tri (IS-05 c.3). Cela change un comportement déjà livré au niveau 1.

### Hypothèses (choix prudents, à confirmer au passage)
- **Sens de Stars** : Stars s'ouvre en décroissant (`DescFirst`). Les lignes sans étoiles forment un bloc en queue en ▼ et en tête en ▲ (IS-05 c.2).
- **Égalités** : la clé de tri de Stars vaut −1 quand `HasStars` est faux. Les égalités gardent l'ordre par défaut d'IS-04 dans les deux sens (`sort.SliceStable` le garantit).
- **Curseur sur `.`** : il suit la ligne sélectionnée (clé `EntryKey` + `Repo`), comme à l'arrivée des lignes. Les autres tables, elles, gardent l'index.
- **`esc` et le filtre `r`** : `esc` n'efface pas le filtre de registre. L'ordre reste : fermer la barre, puis effacer la requête, puis revenir au formulaire, comme au niveau 2. On sort du filtre par `r`.
- **Compteur `Images`** : il continue de compter les lignes visibles après filtres (déjà testé). Les lignes de verdict de l'en-tête de résumé ne dépendent d'aucun filtre.
- **Ordre des arrêts de `r`** : au niveau 1, il suit l'ordre du formulaire (`b.searchKeys`), pas l'ordre d'arrivée, pour rester déterministe.
- **Libellé du jeton** : celui de `registryFilterLabel`, c'est-à-dire l'alias du groupe ou `parent/alias`.
- **`r` sans effet** : `r` est grisé quand il n'y a rien à filtrer. Pas de message en pied de page : c'est un contrôle, pas une action (Rule 130).

### Ce qui existe déjà au niveau 1
Le niveau 1 utilise déjà la barre de `datatable` :
- `/` filtre sur Name et Description (les deux colonnes ont `Search`).
- `:` va dans le champ, `esc` ferme d'abord la barre.
